title: Canada's Eric Bauza, modern voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and others, dead at 46
summary: Eric Bauza of Scarborough, Ont., the Emmy-award winning voice actor best known for the iconic Bugs Bunny, has died.

blocks.text: Toronto
Eric Bauza of Scarborough, Ont., the Emmy-award winning voice actor best known for the iconic Bugs Bunny, has died.
Emmy-award winning voice actor's family said he passed away 'suddenly' in an Instagram post
Canadian voice actor Eric Bauza, who portrayed Looney Tunes characters, dead at 46
Eric Bauza of Scarborough, Ont., the Emmy-award winning voice actor best known for the iconic Bugs Bunny, has died. He was 46.
Bauza's family announced he had passed away "suddenly" in a post to his Instagram profile Sunday night. The family did not say the cause of death, but indicated they would share more at a later time.
A report by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner says Bauza died at his home of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.

Bauza, who was known as a modern successor to original Bugs Bunny voice actor Mel Blanc, grew up watching Bugs Bunny's cartoon exploits at his home in Ontario. In 2020, he was charged with bringing the character to life in all his carrot-munching, prank-pulling glory for HBO Max's Looney Tunes Cartoons, which ran for six seasons.
"It is a dream come true," Bauza told host Ismaila Alfa on CBC Radio's Metro Morning at the time.

In addition to Bugs Bunny, Bauza voiced multiple other characters including Daffy Duck, Tweety Bird and Marvin the Martian. It took two auditions and plenty of practice to land the parts, he told Alfa.
Canadian behind the voice of Bugs Bunny
In 2020, he gave his advice to young voice actors, telling them to remember that, at its base, it's "about the acting, first."
"You have to instill a performance that's grounded in reality," he said.
Among Bauza's credits are such TV shows as The Looney Tunes Show, SpongeBob SquarePants and Bob's Burgers.
He also voiced Foghorn Leghorn, Road Runner, and others in this year's Coyote vs. Acme movie.
Bauza was a regular on the convention circuit, and spoke on a panel at Lightbox Expo in Pasadena, Calif., the day before he died.
Tributes pour in
Jerry Beck, an animation historian, moderated that panel and wrote about it on the website Animation Scoop after Bauza's death.

"He was vibrant and alive," Beck wrote. "To demonstrate a classic piece of Looney Tunes comedy he performed as Bugs Bunny doing the square dance call from 'Hillbilly Hare', while the classic cartoon ran on a large screen beside us, to a packed room full of hopeful artists, cartoonists and budding voice over performers."

Bauza was a "unique voice talent," who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks chair Channing Dungey and Warner Bros. Pictures Animation president and chief creative officer Bill Damaschke said in a post on Instagram Monday.

"Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones," the two said. "Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life."
In an online tribute, fellow voice actor Josh Keaton said Bauza was a gifted and humble performer, and remembered him for having a warm smile and always being sincere.
"He let his talent speak for itself and made everyone feel like he was their biggest fan," Keaton said on social media.
"He will always be a legend but I'm devastated that I'll never be able to give him a hug, or hear him joke or see him smile again."
